sections.title: How is the spread calculated?
paragraphs: Subtract IORB from SOFR in percentage units, then multiply by 100. Here, (3.88 − 3.90) × 100 = −2 bp. One basis point is 0.01 percentage point. Comparing a new SOFR observation with an older IORB value can create a misleading spread, so Seiche uses dates shared by both series.

SOFR measures the cost of overnight borrowing secured by Treasury collateral. IORB is the rate the Federal Reserve pays on eligible reserve balances. They describe different instruments and counterparties, which is why their difference is informative but is not a risk-free arbitrage offer.

sections.title: How should a researcher read it?
paragraphs: A value below zero means this broad Treasury repo rate is below IORB on the matched date. A value above zero means repo borrowing is more expensive than that administered reserve rate. Read the spread with reserve balances, repo volumes, distribution percentiles, facility use and calendar effects.
In the five observations from 28 September through 2 October in this capture, SOFR was above IORB on zero days. That is a description of the retained sample, not a prediction for the next session.

pages.title: Why is SOFR above IORB?
pages.answer: It was not above IORB in the latest paired observation retained here: on 2 October 2026, SOFR was 3.88% and IORB was 3.90%, a −2 bp spread. When the spread does turn positive, it can reflect pressure on secured funding or on the intermediaries moving cash and collateral. The spread alone cannot tell you which mechanism caused it.

sections.title: Why does the comparison have no automatic ceiling?
paragraphs: IORB is available to eligible institutions holding reserve balances. Repo markets connect a broader set of cash borrowers and lenders, with collateral, counterparty and balance-sheet constraints. Cash does not move between every participant without cost or limit.

Greater demand to finance Treasury holdings, changes in cash availability and limits on intermediary capacity can affect repo pricing. Month-end or quarter-end balance-sheet management can coincide with price pressure. Establishing a cause requires evidence about the particular date; a calendar label alone is not proof.

sections.title: What would distinguish a brief move from broader pressure?
paragraphs: Check whether the positive spread persists across observations and whether the upper tail of repo rates, repo volumes and facility use move with it. Compare the Treasury General Account and reserve balances using their own publication dates. Do not turn a single one-day spike into a bank-failure claim.
This retained desk contains zero positive SOFR–IORB observations out of the five observations ending 2 October. A new observation can change that count without changing the definition of the spread.

pages.title: Are bank reserves scarce or still ample?
pages.answer: The reserve total alone cannot establish whether reserves are scarce or ample. Seiche retained $2,948.09 billion of reserve balances for 30 September 2026, up $17.897 billion over one week. Its separate 2 October observation shows SOFR 2 bp below IORB and zero reported Standing Repo Facility use. Those readings do not support a simple claim of immediate system-wide scarcity, but they do not prove every institution has ample funding.
pages.description: Assess reserve abundance using dated reserve balances, SOFR–IORB and facility use. See why an aggregate dollar threshold cannot settle the question.
pages.boundary: Weekly reserves and daily market rates have different dates. There is no calibrated binary scarcity threshold in this example.

tables.title: The stock and the market signals
tables.note: The reserve stock is the weekly Federal Reserve H.4.1 series; the price and facility readings are daily. Zero reported facility use is not a statement about every institution’s access or need.

sections.title: What does “ample” mean in practice?
paragraphs: In an ample-reserves operating framework, administered rates help control short-term interest rates without frequent changes in reserve supply. The relevant question is how funding prices respond as reserve supply and distribution change, not whether the aggregate stock exceeds one fixed number.

A large aggregate balance can coexist with friction at a particular bank or dealer. Payment timing, internal limits, access to facilities and the distribution of balances affect whether available cash reaches the participant that needs it.

sections.title: How to read this particular example
paragraphs: The retained weekly reserve stock increased, while the later matched repo spread was negative and reported SRF use was zero. These are observations from different clocks. Together they provide context, not a contemporaneous causal test or a safety verdict.

A useful follow-up is to watch persistence: several observations of wider funding spreads, changing rate distributions and facility use carry a different research question from a one-day movement. Seiche keeps missing or aging evidence visible rather than treating it as reassurance.
